narrative.summary: ASEAN's AI work is led by its digital ministers (ADGMIN), who adopted a voluntary regional guide on AI governance and ethics in 2024 and welcomed an expanded guide on generative AI in 2025, and set up a Working Group on AI Governance. ASEAN Leaders adopted a declaration establishing an ASEAN AI Safety Network in October 2025. Science and technology ministers adopted a statement on AI in 2024, and ASEAN has adopted joint AI statements with the United States (leaders, 2024) and Japan (digital ministers, 2026). All of these texts are voluntary and non-binding.
lead_institutions: ASEAN Digital Senior Officials' Meeting (ADGSOM) Working Group on AI Governance (WG-AI)
ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Science, Technology and Innovation (AMMSTI)

instruments.english_title: Expanded ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics – Generative AI
instruments.issuing_authority: ASEAN (ASEAN Secretariat); developed by all ASEAN Member States
instruments.publisher_name: ASEAN (ASEAN Secretariat); developed by all ASEAN Member States
instruments.current_status: Published by the ASEAN Secretariat. The Guide states that it was developed collaboratively by all ASEAN Member States and is to be applied on a voluntary basis. The Bangkok Digital Declaration adopted by ASEAN digital ministers on 17 January 2025 refers to it.
instruments.summary: Supplement to the 2024 ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics that gives ASEAN policymakers a policy-focused view of the risks and opportunities of generative AI. It recommends coordinated, pro-innovation regional actions across nine areas and draws on national and international practice.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing generative & agentic ai, responsible ai & ethics, government ai governance.

instruments.official_title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics
instruments.english_title: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics
instruments.current_status: Endorsed by the 4th ADGMIN (Singapore, 1-2 February 2024); voluntary.
instruments.summary: Voluntary regional guide setting seven guiding principles (transparency, fairness, security, reliability, human-centricity, privacy, accountability) and a governance framework for organisations designing and deploying AI. It also gives national-level recommendations for ASEAN Member States.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Regional voluntary framework for member-state AI governance.
instruments.evidence_reference: Status note: Publication date source (date audit 2026-10-13): ASEAN Joint Media Statement of the 4th ADGMIN, 'Singapore, 1 - 2 February 2024': 'the Meeting endorsed the ASEAN Guide on Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance and Ethics' (asean.org page dated February 2, 2024). Guide PDF itself states only 'Copyright 2024'; asean.org book page 'Year 2024'. | Research pass 2026-10-21: Existing record checked; no change. The 6th ADGMIN Joint Media Statement (16 Jan 2026, para 5) refers to it as 'ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics (2024)', consistent with the record.

instruments.issuing_authority: ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Science, Technology and Innovation (AMMSTI)
instruments.publisher_name: ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Science, Technology and Innovation (AMMSTI)
instruments.summary: Ministerial statement by ASEAN science, technology and innovation ministers on AI. It commits to sharing practices on AI skills and workforce upskilling, investing in regional AI infrastructure such as data centres and computing, cooperating on large language models reflecting local languages and cultures, strengthening data governance, and upholding ethical principles such as transparency, fairness and accountability.
instruments.current_status: Adopted at the 20th AMMSTI on 7 June 2024. Political statement; non-binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date from the document: 'Adopted at AMMSTI-20, 7 June 2024'. Read via WebFetch 2026-10-21.

instruments.official_title: ASEAN-U.S. Leaders' Statement on Promoting Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: ASEAN-U.S. Leaders' Statement on Promoting Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Joint statement of ASEAN and United States leaders on AI. It prioritises collaboration on AI governance and capacity building within the ASEAN-U.S. Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, commits to strengthening the safety, security and trustworthiness of AI systems, including through secure ICT ecosystems and cybersecurity collaboration, supports interoperable AI governance approaches and frameworks, commits to help close AI divides, and to empower youth, women, rural populations and vulnerable communities to participate in the digital economy.
instruments.current_status: Adopted in Vientiane, Lao PDR, on 11 October 2024 on the occasion of the 12th ASEAN-United States Summit.
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption line in PDF: 'ADOPTED in Vientiane, Lao PDR, on the 11th of October in the Year Two Thousand and Twenty-Four.' Also noted in 5th ADGMIN JMS para 20. | Independent check 2026-10-21: text does not say 'non-binding'; summary slightly merges two commitments (closing AI divides; empowering youth, women, rural and vulnerable communities)

instruments.official_title: Bangkok Digital Declaration: Secure, Innovative, Inclusive: Shaping ASEAN's Digital Future
instruments.summary: Declaration of ASEAN digital ministers on the region's digital agenda. Its AI commitments call for regional research and investment in emerging technologies including AI and cooperation on governance standards, task the ASEAN Working Group on AI Governance (WG-AI) with facilitating trusted development and deployment of generative AI, and widen the WG-AI's role in supporting ASEAN work on AI policy, governance, safety, laws, regulations and standards.
instruments.current_status: Adopted at the 5th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting (ADGMIN) in Bangkok, Thailand, on 17 January 2025.
instruments.evidence_reference: Included because operative paras 6-7 are dedicated AI commitments (mandate of WG-AI); AI is 3 of 14 operative paras overall. Date: document states adoption at the 5th ADGMIN, Bangkok, 17 January 2025 (meeting 16-17 January 2025). Borderline for 'dedicated AI commitment' test - editor may drop.

instruments.official_title: Declaration on the Establishment of an ASEAN AI Safety Network (ASEAN AI SAFE)
instruments.english_title: Declaration on the Establishment of an ASEAN AI Safety Network (ASEAN AI Safe)
instruments.summary: Leaders' declaration establishing the ASEAN AI Safety Network as a voluntary, non-binding regional mechanism for AI safety. The network is to exchange good practice, support research and capacity building, build multi-stakeholder partnerships and work with external partners, coherently with the ASEAN digital senior officials and the Working Group on AI Governance. Digital ministers are to define its functions and operating model, with Malaysia as lead proponent.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by ASEAN Member States at the 47th ASEAN Summit, Kuala Lumpur, 26 October 2025. The declaration states the network is voluntary and non-binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption line in PDF: 'DONE in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia this Twenty Sixth Day of October in the Year Two Thousand and Twenty-Five'. 6th ADGMIN JMS para 5 notes the adoption.

instruments.official_title: ASEAN–Japan Digital Ministers' Joint Statement on Promoting Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: ASEAN–Japan Digital Ministers' Joint Statement on Promoting Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: 5th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting with Japan (ADGMIN+Japan)
instruments.publisher_name: 5th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting with Japan (ADGMIN+Japan)
instruments.summary: Joint statement of ASEAN and Japanese digital ministers on AI. It commits to strengthening AI safety, security and trustworthiness through shared governance, including risk-based approaches in high-impact sectors such as health, education, finance and public administration; to expanding AI capacity building; and to promoting human-centred AI that protects privacy and intellectual property, counters disinformation and supports trusted cross-border data flows.
instruments.current_status: Adopted in Hanoi, Viet Nam, on 15 January 2026 at the 5th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting with Japan (ADGMIN+Japan); published by Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications.
instruments.evidence_reference: Full text hosted by co-adopter Japan (Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications); no asean.org copy located (search budget exhausted). ASEAN's own 6th ADGMIN JMS (asean.org, 16 Jan 2026, para 18) records its adoption. Adoption line: 'ADOPTED in Hanoi, Viet Nam on the 15th of January in the Year Two Thousand and TwentySix.' Editor may prefer to hold as lead until an asean.org copy is found. | Independent check 2026-10-21: text does not say 'non-binding'; meeting is named on the MIC page as the 5th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting with Japan (ADGMIN+Japan); statement prints 'Hanoi'

instruments.official_title: Hanoi Digital Declaration – "Adaptive ASEAN: From Connectivity to Connected Intelligence"
instruments.english_title: Hanoi Digital Declaration – Adaptive ASEAN: From Connectivity to Connected Intelligence
instruments.summary: Declaration of ASEAN digital ministers on moving from connectivity to 'connected intelligence'. It includes a dedicated commitment to deepen cooperation on AI, led by the Working Group on AI Governance with support from the ASEAN AI Safety Network, and refers to AI in digital infrastructure, workforce skills and green transformation.
instruments.current_status: Adopted at the 6th ASEAN Digital Ministers' Meeting in Ha Noi on 16 January 2026. Political declaration; non-binding.
instruments.evidence_reference: Adoption line in PDF: 'ADOPTED this Declaration at the 6th ADGMIN in Ha Noi, Viet Nam on 16 January 2026.' (PDF filename says 14Jan2026 - ignored.) Operative para 8 is the dedicated AI commitment; AI appears in 4 of 10 operative paras.
